# The `subagent` frame — the contract `ai.js` is built against

PRD 6.3. The parent's stream carries `subagent` frames; the child's full
transcript is inspectable (F8). This document is the wire contract between
the API's emitter (`chats/prompts.py`, `chats/tools/subagents.py`) and the
`ai.js` on the CDN, written in the shape of `ai-question-frame.md` because
the hazards are the same hazards: a frame that must survive `finishStream`'s
wholesale trail replacement, a step old clients render through a live
markdown sink, a fold that must collapse a replayed pair into one row, and a
chrome surface where the **absence** of presentational fields is the
security control.

Since PRD 7.7 the shape below is also DECLARED on the server, in
`chats/frames.py`, where `SUBAGENT_KEYS` and the four states now live and
where `prompts.py` re-exports them from. The two are not left to agree by
hand: `tests/ui/test_frame_drift.py` reads §1's key list and its state
comment out of THIS FILE and compares them to that registry, so a key or a
state added on one side and not the other fails. What it checks is the
vocabulary, and only that — everything else here is reasoning, which is what
a document is for and what no test can hold.

## 0. The one-paragraph version

A spawn is **two steps sharing one call id**. The `kind:"tool"` step is
6.1's, untouched: it is the approval row (`pending` state) and the refusal
sentence on every shipped ai.js, and `_tool_frames` stays its only writer.
The `kind:"subagent"` step is the DELEGATION: the child chat's identity, its
lifecycle, and the handle the transcript panel opens. They coexist because
the fold keys on kind AND id. The frame and step are one dict with different
discriminators, produced by one allowlist (`_subagent_fields`), emitted from
inside the spawn dispatch through the output sink's out-of-band seam
(`prompts.emit_subagent`), replayed by `tail_message`'s settled branch, and
closed at every settle by `settle_subagent_steps`.

## 1. The shape

```jsonc
// frame:  {"type": "subagent", ...fields}
// step:   {"kind": "subagent", ...fields}
SUBAGENT_KEYS = ("id", "chat", "reply", "state", "title", "text",
                 "spawned_at")

{
  "id":         "call_abc",     // the spawn call's call_id — stamped by the
                                // emit seam from the live sink, shared with
                                // the tool step; the fold key with `kind`
  "chat":       "<uuid>",       // the child chat's id — THE inspection handle
  "reply":      "<uuid>",       // the child's reply id — what a live tail
                                // would follow (the 6.7 seam)
  "state":      "running",      // running | done | failed | stopped
  "title":      "Reconcile…",   // the task, capped 120, control-stripped,
                                // whitespace-collapsed (the child chat's own
                                // title, one cap in three places)
  "text":       "A sub-agent is working on: Reconcile…",  // §3
  "spawned_at": "2026-08-15T10:00:00Z"                    // utc_stamp
}
```

All seven keys are always present. Deliberate namings:

* `reply`, **not** `message` — on the question step `message` means "the
  PARENT reply id to POST the answer to". This step has nothing to POST, and
  reusing the name for "the CHILD's reply" would be a semantic collision
  across kinds.
* No parent-message key at all: inspection is a GET addressed by `chat`.
* `cost_micros` is **RESERVED** for 6.7's cost surfacing. No server emits it
  yet; the client fold's allowlist already carries it, because a key absent
  from that list is one no shipped client will ever store. It will be a
  PLATFORM-written integer (micros), never model text. Key-set equality
  tests pin the seven server keys and tolerate the reserved key's absence.
  Identity, not figures, is the durable seam: a figure frozen onto the step
  at settle is guaranteed stale for an abandoned child, whose own
  `_settle_stopped` bills after the step's last fold — so the step must
  never be the source of truth for money.

## 2. The states, and exactly what produces each

| State | Produced by | `text` |
|---|---|---|
| `running` | child rows written, `_run_child` about to start | "A sub-agent is working on: {title}" |
| `done` | child settled DONE on its own — an empty answer is done, not failed | "A sub-agent finished: {title}" |
| `failed` | the child ROW says FAILED | "A sub-agent could not finish: {title}" |
| `stopped` | `stopped_at` on the child row (a person's stop cascaded in, or the wall clock), **or** the wait was abandoned (grace expired) | "A sub-agent was stopped: {title}" |

Binding rules:

* **The terminal state comes from the CHILD ROW, never from dispatch's
  `ok`.** The handler deliberately returns ok for a child that ran and
  failed ("a sub-agent that came back with little to say is not a tool
  failure"), so the TOOL step reads completed beside a `failed` subagent
  step. That divergence is pinned by a test as a pair; the subagent step is
  the honest one.
* **There is deliberately no state named `pending`** — on this surface a
  pending trail step means *a human must act* (the approval buttons), and a
  sub-agent needs nothing from a human. `spawned` is collapsed into
  `running`: there is no moment between them a client can act on
  differently.
* **Forward compatibility**: every reader treats the state as an allowlist.
  Anything unrecognised renders settled and inert — never running, never
  actionable. That is what lets 6.7 add a state or a key.
* **A refusal emits no subagent frame and folds no subagent step.** Every
  refusal raises `ToolError` before the emit point and lands on the tool
  step as `error` with the pinned sentence; a subagent step beside it would
  say the same sentence twice one row apart, with no chat to inspect. This
  includes the late `TOOLS_OFF` refusal after the child's rows exist: the
  stillborn child (a brief, an empty DONE reply) stays unreferenced — it
  spent nothing.

## 3. The old-client `text` rule (5.2's lesson, binding here)

An old ai.js drops the FRAME (flat `handleEvent` chain, no default branch)
and renders the STEP through `content.innerHTML = renderMarkdown(s.text ||
s.kind || "")` — a live markdown sink. Therefore:

* `text` is a top-level, always-present, PLATFORM-composed sentence. Never
  rename it, never nest it, never add a `text`-keyed sub-object to this step
  later.
* The only model-authored content inside it is the task title, capped at 120
  and control-stripped at the emitter (`_step_title`). **This is a genuinely
  new markdown surface on old clients** — unlike the question's `text`, the
  task title is not already in the bubble — and the residual risk is
  accepted for the question contract's reasons: the fleet's `renderMarkdown`
  escapes first and gates every href through `safeHref`, so a
  markdown-shaped title is a rendered link at worst, never script. The cap
  and strip are mutation-tested against the literal.
* Every rewrite of `state` rewrites `text` with it — `text` is the only
  thing an old client will ever read. The settle close writes "This reply
  ended while a sub-agent was still running: {title}".
* Sub-agents ship dark, so no old SERVER ever emits this frame — but old
  cached CLIENTS meet the step the day a deployment turns the flag on, and
  the fallback sentence is what they print forever.

## 4. Fold, replay, and the settle close

* **Folded on `(kind, id)`, last write wins**, both sides. The kind is in
  the key because the subagent step and the spawn's tool step share the
  call id — the rule's stated case. A reconnect mid-delegation replays
  `running` and then the terminal frame for one id and must end with one
  step.
* **The client fold is an allowlist** over `SUBAGENT_KEYS` plus the reserved
  `cost_micros`: `kind` is client-owned and never taken from the wire,
  `type` is dropped, `_`-keys are unwritable. Mutation-tested: a widened
  fold lets a frame re-kind the step into the approval row's shape.
* **No `mergeServerActivity` clause for this kind** — unlike an answer, the
  client never holds delegation state the server lacks (there is no client
  POST), so `finishStream`'s wholesale trail replacement is already correct.
  Do not add a merge "for symmetry".
* **The replay arm** in `tail_message`'s settled branch re-emits the step as
  a frame; a settled reply never replays `running` (rewritten to `stopped`
  as the read-time backstop). A kind missing from that loop does not fail —
  it VANISHES on reload.
* **The settle-time close is the sixth registration point.**
  `settle_subagent_steps` runs inside `close_open_steps`, so every
  transition out of `LIVE_STATES` — the finalize, the stop, the failure
  path, the idle settle, `close_orphaned_pause` — rewrites a stranded
  `running` step to `stopped` with its text. It is what covers a handler
  that raises before its terminal emit.

## 5. The live story (decided: state-plus-handle)

The `running` frame is emitted **after the last refusal point, immediately
before `_run_child`** — that position is load-bearing: earlier strands a
running step on a refusal; later leaves the stream silent while money is
spent. The terminal frame is emitted after the child row is read back.

The panel gets liveness by *fetching*: on open, and again whenever the
parent's subagent step folds a new state. Live-tailing the child's stream
inside the panel is **rejected for 6.3** (a second producer into a
prefix-invariant buffer server-side; a second SSE and a recursive renderer
client-side) and named as 6.7's seam — the child's `messages/<reply>/stream/`
endpoint is already ownership-scoped and reachable, so the tail costs no new
API when it is wanted. Periodic mid-run status refolds ("working —
<child step title>") were considered and deferred with it: they need a
second model-influenced key and a threaded-path-only test, and the fold
machinery makes them a purely additive change later.

## 6. Inspection is read-only, structurally

The owner reads a child end to end through endpoints that already existed:
chat detail (provenance: `parent`, `spawned_by_message`, `depth`), messages
list (the transcript, `activity` published raw), message stream. Everybody
else gets the detail 404; the messages list answers `200 []` for any unowned
chat — deliberately NOT changed to 404 for children, which would create an
existence oracle. **The chat detail 404 is the not-found signal**, and the
panel reads it that way.

Writes are closed server-side in the same release that makes children
navigable — `parent__isnull=True` in `MessageView.perform_create` and
`StreamRepliesView._validate_chat_id`, `parent_id` refusals in
`ChatView.update`/`perform_destroy` — all answering the queue's 404. A
composer on a child would collide with the parent's blocked worker,
`close_orphaned_pause`, and `messages/latest/`; a child can never hold a
claimable pause (dispatch refuses ASK for sub-agents), so the panel builds
no answer or approval controls. The one interaction deliberately left open
is **Stop**: `StopView` resolves a child reply, which is 6.7's "this child
is spending — stop it" seam.

The panel is a drawer beside the parent conversation — children are not
navigation-level objects (no list row, no history entry). A pasted child URL
renders the conversation read-only: composer hidden, one banner; on an old
cached ai.js the send simply 404s, which is the acceptable degradation.

## 7. What the step must NOT carry

* No presentational field, ever — no `icon`, `glyph`, `variant`, `color`,
  `style`, `class`, and no URL or href of any kind. `icon()` builds
  `"ti ti-" + name` with no scrub; **stating the absence is the security
  control**. The state→glyph map is a table ai.js owns (`SUBAGENT_GLYPHS`),
  keyed by a checked state, and every glyph in it was already in pre-6.3
  icon sheets (`tool`, `circle-check`, `circle-x`, `clock` — pinned by a
  source-level test).
* No model free text beyond the capped title — no `answer`, no task body.
  The answer's head reaches the person through the tool step's capped
  `summary`; the full truth is the transcript.
* `chat`/`reply` are opaque ids: UUID-validated, used only as path segments,
  never concatenated into HTML, classes or icon names.

## 8. Known gaps, stated so nobody rediscovers them

* **A tree-budget cut mid-child leaves no durable trace in the child's
  transcript**: `TREE_QUOTA_ERROR` is emitted as a live frame only, the
  child finalizes DONE with partial content and an empty error column, and
  the buffer — the only copy of the sentence — is reclaimed. The parent's
  summary then reads "The sub-agent answered: …". Pre-existing (6.2), out of
  6.3's scope; fixing it means writing the refusal onto the child row or its
  trail, and touching 6.2's pinned-sentence tests.
* **The tool step reads completed for a failed child** (deliberate 6.1
  behaviour, see §2). The subagent step is the honest pair.
* **Panel reads trigger the incognito lazy purge** — opening a child's
  transcript is "the next GET to another chat id" and hard-deletes a stale
  incognito session, like opening any chat. Kept: consistent with the
  existing contract, not special-cased.
* **An abandoned child's step is frozen at `stopped`** while the child
  settles its own row moments later; the transcript, not the step, is the
  truth of where it got to. If the flicker ever matters, the panel's refetch
  shows the settled row.
